definition: Coordinated network of independent, bounded, versioned contexts. Context states, not agents, are the fundamental units.

contexts.title: SCS charter and operating boundary
contexts.purpose: Define the swarm as a context-state coordination protocol and keep production implementation deferred until evidence supports it.
contexts.change_note: Seeded from user-confirmed definition and operating-model correction.

contexts.title: Input and task consumption protocol
contexts.purpose: Specify how new information enters, is normalized, related, prioritized, processed, verified, and recorded.
open_questions: Add replayable intake scenarios with positive, duplicate, conflict, inaccessible-source, and unsafe-input cases.
contexts.change_note: Initial operating contract; subject to test-driven improvement.

contexts.title: Repository engineering swarm demonstrator
contexts.purpose: Use this repository's real files, commits, contracts, and tests to exercise the context-state workflow without a backend.
open_questions: Build evidence-backed repository inventory and dependency map.
Add replayable task and context transition scenarios.
Identify inconsistencies among reference artifacts and current operating rules.
contexts.change_note: First target context for ongoing real work.

contexts.title: Production backend selection
contexts.purpose: Keep backend choice out of scope until repository-native swarm behavior and implementation contracts have matured.
open_questions: Reopen only after implementation-readiness criteria have evidence.
contexts.change_note: Deliberately deferred; no provisioning or backend selection.

work_items.title: Audit existing repository artifacts against the repository-native operating model

priority.rationale: Detect contradictory or premature artifacts before extending the protocol.

acceptance_criteria: Every current artifact is classified as current, reference-only, superseded, or deferred.
Contradictions are recorded with paths and a proposed disposition.

work_items.title: Add replayable intake and context-state transition cases

priority.rationale: Turn the intake contract into observable behavior before implementing a runtime.

acceptance_criteria: Contradictory claims produce a conflict state.
Inaccessible sources produce a blocked/limited result, not fabricated data.
Accepted context changes record evidence and a new version.
required_evidence: Executable tests or replayable scenario fixtures

work_items.title: Populate the repository engineering context with evidence-backed inventory

priority.rationale: Use actual repository artifacts as the initial dataset, rather than synthetic sample data alone.

acceptance_criteria: Canonical repository tree and current branch head are recorded.
Each artifact has a path, purpose, and status.
Known limitations and unanswered implementation questions are recorded.
Claims link to source paths or commit evidence.
required_evidence: Inventory artifact committed to the repository
